newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Weaker in line with bearish crude.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Weaker in line with bearish crude.

text.p: The recent plunge in Brent crude prices kept the the fuel oil market weak on Monday and traders expected soft crude values to continue adding further pressure to prices.
"It's usually very quiet on Monday and especially when crude is weak, there are very few activities," said one trader.
The 380-cst grade high sulphur fuel oil traded at $92.5 per tonne for May 2-6 lifting, compared with last Wednesday's traded level of $94.50, traders said.
"There are still some 180-cst cargoes coming in so there is no rush to buy," said one trader.

Brent rebounded slightly on Monday to last trade at up 25 cents at $17.88. on Friday, May Brent crude lost 50 cents to close at $17.68 per barrel on the International Petroleum Exchange--taking its loses for the week to $1.43.
Overall sentiment was sluggish, with no keen interest seen after a local trader, who was expected to support the market, failed to emerge since late last week.
A major said he was still seeking to buy for May lifting.
The LSWR market remained gloomy, with offers heard at $16.25 per tonne, due to ample supplies and a lack of fresh demand from China and Japan, traders said.
Indonesia's state oil company, Pertamina, is expected to have more than four million barrels of LSWR for April loading, traders said.
"Sentiment is very bearish with such ample supply," said one trader.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
